024//@formatter:off
025/**
026 * The main entry point and configuration of RainbowGum logging.
027 * <p>
028 * RainbowGum logging loads configuration through the service loader. While you can
029 * manually set RainbowGum using {@link #set(Supplier)} it is better to register
030 * implementations through the ServiceLoader so that RainbowGum will load prior to any
031 * external logging.
032 * <p>
033 * To register a custom RainbowGum:
034 *
035 *
036{@snippet class="snippets.RainbowGumProviderExample" region="provider" :
037
038class RainbowGumProviderExample implements RainbowGumProvider {
039
040        @Override
041        public Optional<RainbowGum> provide(LogConfig config) {
042
043                Integer bufferSize = config.properties() //
044                        .forKey("logging.custom.async.bufferSize")
045                        .ofInt()
046                        .or(1024)
047                        .validateNow(RainbowGumProviderExample.class);
048
049                LogProvider<LogOutput> output = (name, cfg) -> cfg.properties()
050                        .forKey("logging.custom.output")
051                        .ofProvider(LogOutput::of)
052                        .or(LogOutput.ofStandardOut())
053                        .validateNow(RainbowGumProviderExample.class)
054                        .provide(name, cfg);
055
056                var gum = RainbowGum.builder() //
057                        .route(r -> {
058                                r.publisher(PublisherFactory //
059                                        .async() //
060                                        .bufferSize(bufferSize) //
061                                        .build());
062                                r.appender("console", a -> {
063                                        a.output(output);
064                                });
065                                r.level(Level.INFO);
066                        })
067                        .build();
068
069                return Optional.of(gum);
070        }
071
072}
073}
074 * <p>
075 * <strong>Initialization order</strong> - most of the actual work happens in
076 * {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()}, {@link LogRouter.Router.Builder}, and
077 * {@code LogAppenderRegistry}; this is the exact sequence for anyone debugging a
078 * configuration or writing a {@link RainbowGumServiceProvider.RainbowGumProvider}:
079 * <ol>
080 * <li>{@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} builds the shared {@link LogConfig}:
081 * <ol>
082 * <li>Resolve the {@link ServiceRegistry} (default: a new empty one) and
083 * {@link LogProperties} - manually added
084 * {@link RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider}s, else (if a
085 * {@link java.util.ServiceLoader} was supplied) SPI-discovered ones, with system
086 * properties always layered in as a final fallback.</li>
087 * <li>Build {@link LogAlerts} and {@link LogMetrics} from properties.</li>
088 * <li>Build the global level resolver ({@code logging.level.*} and
089 * {@code logging.group.*}, plus anything added directly on the builder).</li>
090 * <li>Construct the {@link LogConfig} itself - this is also where a few
091 * process-wide flags get latched (config change support, the appender lock, and
092 * thread-local-disabled globals) and the default output/encoder/publisher
093 * registries are created.</li>
094 * <li>Run every {@link RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} (manually added,
095 * then SPI-discovered), highest {@linkplain RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator#priority()
096 * priority} first. A configurator returning {@code false} is retried in a later
097 * pass (see {@link RainbowGumServiceProvider#PASSES}) - useful if it depends on
098 * another configurator running first.</li>
099 * <li>Start {@link LogAlerts} - deliberately last, so a configurator's own alert
100 * listener is already registered before alerts decides whether an unobserved
101 * error should refuse startup.</li>
102 * </ol>
103 * </li>
104 * <li>{@link Builder#build()} builds each named {@link LogRouter.Router} (a single
105 * route named {@value LogProperties#DEFAULT_NAME}, unless {@code logging.routes}
106 * names several) via {@link LogRouter.Router.Builder}'s own (package-private)
107 * {@code build()}:
108 * <ol>
109 * <li>Resolve route flags ({@code logging.route.<name>.flags}).</li>
110 * <li>Build a route-scoped level resolver: anything configured directly on the
111 * route builder, layered over {@code logging.route.<name>.level.*}, falling back
112 * to the global level resolver from step 1 (skipped entirely if the route flag
113 * {@code IGNORE_GLOBAL_LEVEL_RESOLVER} is set) - and finally to {@code INFO} if
114 * nothing at all resolves a level.</li>
115 * <li>Resolve appenders - only if none were added programmatically on the route
116 * builder (that check is all-or-nothing: adding even one appender in code skips
117 * property-based resolution entirely). See <strong>Appender resolution</strong>
118 * below.</li>
119 * <li>Resolve the publisher - {@code logging.route.<name>.publisher}, falling
120 * back to a synchronous publisher if unset.</li>
121 * <li>Hand the resolved appenders to the publisher and register the publisher in
122 * the {@link ServiceRegistry}.</li>
123 * </ol>
124 * </li>
125 * <li>{@link #start()} starts the root router, which starts each route's
126 * publisher, which starts each of its appenders, which starts its output (e.g.
127 * opening a file).</li>
128 * </ol>
129 * <strong>Appender resolution</strong> - the part most often mistaken for a bug,
130 * since no appenders are ever added programmatically in the common case:
131 * <ol>
132 * <li>{@code logging.route.<name>.appenders} names the route's appenders; for the
133 * {@value LogProperties#DEFAULT_NAME} route only, a missing value falls back to
134 * the unprefixed {@code logging.appenders}.</li>
135 * <li>If that is <em>still</em> missing: for the default route only, the list
136 * defaults to {@code [file, console]} if {@code logging.file.name} (or Spring
137 * Boot's convention) is set, otherwise just {@code [console]}. A non-default
138 * route with no appenders configured anywhere is a startup failure, not a silent
139 * no-op.</li>
140 * <li>Each named appender then resolves independently. {@code file} and
141 * {@code console} are the two built-in special cases, each with its own output
142 * property/fallback ({@code logging.file.name} then
143 * {@code logging.appender.file.output} for {@code file};
144 * {@code logging.appender.console.output} falling back to standard-out for
145 * {@code console}). Any other name is fully generic:
146 * {@code logging.appender.<name>.output}/{@code .encoder}/{@code .flags}/
147 * {@code .type}, with the output's own URI scheme choosing which registered
148 * {@link LogOutput.OutputProvider} builds it.</li>
149 * <li>An output can supply its own encoder by implementing
150 * {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder} (rare, e.g. some structured outputs): with
151 * {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder.Policy#MANDATORY} that encoder is used as-is
152 * and the {@code .encoder} property is never consulted (configuring one anyway
153 * is a startup failure); with {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder.Policy#DEFAULT}
154 * it is only a fallback and the {@code .encoder} property, if set, still wins.
155 * An output that does not implement {@link LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder} at all is
156 * unaffected - the {@code .encoder} property (or the registry's default for the
157 * output's type) always applies.</li>
158 * </ol>
159 */
160//@formatter:on
161@SuppressWarnings("InvalidInlineTag")
162public sealed interface RainbowGum extends AutoCloseable, LogEventLogger {
163
164        /**
165         * Gets the currently statically bound RainbowGum and will try to load and find one if
166         * there is none currently bound. <strong> This is a blocking operation as in locks
167         * are used and will block indefinitely till a gum has loaded. </strong> If that is
168         * not desired see {@link #getOrNull()}.
169         * @return current RainbowGum or new loaded one.
170         */
171        public static RainbowGum of() {
172                return RainbowGumHolder.get();
173        }
174
175        /**
176         * Gets the currently statically bound RainbowGum or <code>null</code> if none are
177         * <strong>finished binding</strong>. Unlike {@link #of()} this will never load or
178         * start an instance but rather just gets the currently bound one. It will also never
179         * block and does not wait if one is currently being loaded.
180         * @return current RainbowGum or <code>null</code>
181         */
182        public static @Nullable RainbowGum getOrNull() {
183                return RainbowGumHolder.current();
184        }
185
186        /**
187         * Provides the service loader default based RainbowGum.
188         * @return RainbowGum.
189         */
190        public static RainbowGum defaults() {
191                return RainbowGumServiceProvider.provide();
192        }
193
194        /**
195         * Creates a RainbowGum that will <strong>ALWAYS</strong> use the global router.
196         * @param config config.
197         * @return rainbow gum that always uses global router.
198         */
199        public static RainbowGum queued(LogConfig config) {
200                return new SimpleRainbowGum(config, LogRouter.global(), UUID.randomUUID());
201        }
202
203        /**
204         * Sets the global default RainbowGum. The supplied {@link RainbowGum} must not
205         * already be started.
206         * @param supplier the supplier will be memoized when {@linkplain Supplier#get()
207         * accessed} and {@link RainbowGum#start()} will be called.
208         */
209        public static void set(Supplier<RainbowGum> supplier) {
210                RainbowGumHolder.set(supplier);
211        }
212
213        /**
214         * Subscribes to notification of a new RainbowGum becoming the globally bound one (see
215         * {@link #set(Supplier)}, {@link #set(RainbowGum)}, {@link Builder#set()}). This is
216         * primarily for components like SLF4J's logger factory that are themselves
217         * bootstrapped once (often before "the real" RainbowGum has loaded, e.g. a
218         * framework's own pre-boot sequence) and otherwise have no way of finding out that a
219         * different RainbowGum has since replaced the one they captured.
220         * <p>
221         * Only a {@linkplain java.lang.ref.WeakReference weak reference} to
222         * <code>consumer</code> is retained, so subscribing does not by itself keep the
223         * consumer (or whatever it is attached to) reachable - the caller is responsible for
224         * keeping a strong reference to <code>consumer</code> for as long as it needs to keep
225         * receiving notifications, otherwise it may silently stop being called once garbage
226         * collected.
227         * @param consumer called with the newly bound global RainbowGum. Never called while
228         * any RainbowGum internal lock is held.
229         */
230        public static void onGlobalChange(Consumer<RainbowGum> consumer) {
231                RainbowGumHolder.globalChangePublisher.add(consumer);
232        }
233
234        /**
235         * Sets a Rainbow Gum and provides a supplier that will start it globally.
236         * @param gum that will be set immediatly.
237         * @return supplier that will set, get and start the supplied gum and if it is not the
238         * same will throw {@link IllegalStateException}.
239         */
240        public static Supplier<? extends RainbowGum> set(RainbowGum gum) {
241                UUID instanceId = gum.instanceId();
242                RainbowGum.set(() -> gum);
243                return () -> {
244                        var of = RainbowGum.of();
245                        /*
246                         * TODO this is a hack. The holder lock should be used to make this not
247                         * happen.
248                         */
249                        if (!instanceId.equals(of.instanceId())) {
250                                throw new IllegalStateException("Another rainbow gum registered itself as the global. "
251                                                + "This is rare reace condition and probably a bug");
252                        }
253                        return of;
254                };
255        }
256
257        /**
258         * The config associated with this instance.
259         * @return config.
260         */
261        public LogConfig config();
262
263        /**
264         * The router that will route log messages to publishers.
265         * @return router
266         */
267        public RootRouter router();
268
269        /**
270         * Starts the rainbow gum and returns it. It is returned for try-with usage
271         * convenience.
272         * @return the started RainbowGum.
273         */
274        default RainbowGum start() {
275                router().start(config());
276                return this;
277        }
278
279        /**
280         * Unique id of rainbow gum instance.
281         * @return random id created on creation.
282         */
283        public UUID instanceId();
284
285        /**
286         * Will close the RainbowGum and all registered components as well as removed from the
287         * shutdown hooks. If the rainbow gum is set as global it will no longer be global and
288         * replaced with the bootstrapping in memory queue. {@inheritDoc}
289         */
290        @Override
291        public void close();
292
293        /**
294         * This append call is mainly for testing as it does not avoid making events that do
295         * not need to be made if no logging needs to be done. {@inheritDoc}
296         */
297        @Override
298        default void log(LogEvent event) {
299                var r = router().route(event.loggerName(), event.level());
300                if (r.isEnabled()) {
301                        r.log(event);
302                }
303        }
304
305        /**
306         * Use to build a custom {@link RainbowGum} which will use the {@link LogConfig}
307         * provided by the service loader.
308         * @return builder.
309         */
310        public static Builder builder() {
311                ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> loader = ServiceLoader.load(RainbowGumServiceProvider.class);
312                var config = RainbowGumServiceProvider.provideConfig(loader);
313                return builder(config);
314        }
315
316        /**
317         * Use to build a custom {@link RainbowGum} with supplied config.
318         * @param config the config
319         * @return builder.
320         * @see #builder()
321         */
322        public static Builder builder(LogConfig config) {
323                return new Builder(config);
324        }
325
326        /**
327         * Use to build a custom {@link RainbowGum} with supplied config.
328         * @param config consumer that has first argument as config builder.
329         * @return builder.
330         * @see #builder()
331         * @apiNote this method is for ergonomic fluent reasons.
332         */
333        public static Builder builder(Consumer<? super LogConfig.Builder> config) {
334                var b = LogConfig.builder();
335                config.accept(b);
336                return builder(b.build());
337        }
338
339        /**
340         * RainbowGum Builder.
341         */
342        public class Builder {
343
344                private final LogConfig config;
345
346                private final List<Router> routes = new ArrayList<>();
347
348                private Builder(LogConfig config) {
349                        this.config = config;
350                }
351
352                /**
353                 * Adds a router.
354                 * @param route a router.
355                 * @return builder.
356                 */
357                public Builder route(Router route) {
358                        this.routes.add(route);
359                        return this;
360                }
361
362                /**
363                 * Adds a route by using a consumer of the route builder.
364                 * @param name name of router.
365                 * @param consumer consumer is passed router builder. The consumer does not need
366                 * to call {@link Router#builder(String,LogConfig)}
367                 * @return builder.
368                 * @see io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogRouter.Router.Builder
369                 */
370                public Builder route(String name, Consumer<Router.Builder> consumer) {
371                        var builder = Router.builder(name, config);
372                        consumer.accept(builder);
373                        return route(builder.build());
374                }
375
376                /**
377                 * Adds a route by using a consumer of the route builder.
378                 * @param consumer consumer is passed router builder. The consumer does not need
379                 * to call {@link Router#builder(String,LogConfig)}
380                 * @return builder.
381                 * @see io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogRouter.Router.Builder
382                 */
383                public Builder route(Consumer<Router.Builder> consumer) {
384                        var builder = Router.builder(Router.DEFAULT_ROUTER_NAME, config);
385                        consumer.accept(builder);
386                        return route(builder.build());
387                }
388
389                /**
390                 * Builds an un-started {@link RainbowGum}.
391                 * @return an un-started {@link RainbowGum}.
392                 */
393                public RainbowGum build() {
394                        return build(UUID.randomUUID());
395                }
396
397                /**
398                 * Builds an un-started {@link RainbowGum}.
399                 * @param instanceId unique id for rainbow gum instance.
400                 * @return an un-started {@link RainbowGum}.
401                 */
402                private RainbowGum build(UUID instanceId) {
403                        var routes = this.routes;
404                        var config = this.config;
405                        if (routes.isEmpty()) {
406                                var routeNamesResult = config.properties() //
407                                        .forKey(LogProperties.ROUTES_PROPERTY)
408                                        .ofList()
409                                        .or(List.of());
410                                List<String> routeNames = routeNamesResult.validateNow(Builder.class);
411                                /*
412                                 * Validated as a plain list of names, before any of them is used to build
413                                 * a Router, so a bad name is reported against this list property itself,
414                                 * not deferred until some unrelated {name}-keyed property (e.g. this
415                                 * route's own level) happens to interpolate it first.
416                                 */
417                                LogProperty.Validator.validateNames(LogRouter.class, "route", routeNamesResult, routeNames);
418                                if (routeNames.isEmpty()) {
419                                        routes = List.of(Router.builder(Router.DEFAULT_ROUTER_NAME, config).build());
420                                }
421                                else {
422                                        routes = routeNames.stream().map(n -> Router.builder(n, config).build()).toList();
423                                }
424                        }
425                        var root = InternalRootRouter.of(routes, config);
426                        config.changePublisher().subscribe(c -> {
427                                root.changePublisher().publish(root);
428                        });
429                        return new SimpleRainbowGum(config, root, instanceId);
430                }
431
432                /**
433                 * Builds, starts and sets the RainbowGum as the global one picked up by logging
434                 * facades.
435                 * @return started and set rainbow that can be used in a try-close.
436                 */
437                public RainbowGum set() {
438                        UUID instanceId = UUID.randomUUID();
439                        RainbowGum.set(() -> build(instanceId));
440                        var gum = RainbowGum.of();
441                        /*
442                         * TODO this is a hack. The holder lock should be used to make this not
443                         * happen.
444                         */
445                        if (!instanceId.equals(gum.instanceId())) {
446                                throw new IllegalStateException("Another rainbow gum registered itself as the global. "
447                                                + "This is rare reace condition and probably a bug");
448                        }
449                        return gum;
450                }
451
452                /**
453                 * Removes the currently set Rainbow Gum which will close it if one exists and
454                 * will be replaced by the default provision process if {@link RainbowGum#of()} is
455                 * called before {@link #set()}.
456                 * @apiNote This is largely an internal detail for unit testing the provision
457                 * process.
458                 */
459                public void unset() {
460                        RainbowGumHolder.remove(null);
461                }
462
463                /**
464                 * For returning an optional for the LogProvider contract.
465                 * @return optional that always has a rainbow gum.
466                 * @apiNote this method is for ergonomics.
467                 */
468                public Optional<RainbowGum> optional() {
469                        return Optional.of(this.build());
470                }
471
472                /**
473                 * For returning an optional for the LogProvider contract.
474                 * @param condition condition to check if this rainbow gum should be used.
475                 * @return optional rainbow gum.
476                 * @apiNote this method is for ergonomics.
477                 */
478                public Optional<RainbowGum> optional(Function<? super LogConfig, Boolean> condition) {
479                        var cond = condition.apply(config);
480                        if (cond) {
481                                return Optional.of(this.build());
482                        }
483                        return Optional.empty();
484                }
485
486        }
487
488}
489
490final class RainbowGumHolder {
491
492        /*
493         * TODO perhaps a StampedLock would be better performance wise.
494         */
495        private static final ReentrantReadWriteLock lock = new ReentrantReadWriteLock();
496
497        private static Supplier<RainbowGum> supplier = RainbowGumServiceProvider::provide;
498
499        private static volatile @Nullable RainbowGum rainbowGum = null;
500
501        static final GlobalChangePublisher globalChangePublisher = new GlobalChangePublisher();
502
503        static @Nullable RainbowGum current() {
504                if (lock.readLock().tryLock()) {
505                        try {
506                                return rainbowGum;
507                        }
508                        finally {
509                                lock.readLock().unlock();
510                        }
511                }
512                return null;
513        }
514
515        static RainbowGum get() {
516                lock.readLock().lock();
517                try {
518                        var r = rainbowGum;
519                        if (r != null) {
520                                return r;
521                        }
522                }
523                finally {
524                        lock.readLock().unlock();
525                }
526                if (lock.writeLock().isHeldByCurrentThread()) {
527                        throw new IllegalStateException("RainbowGum component tried to log too early. "
528                                        + "This is usually caused by dependencies calling logging.");
529                }
530                RainbowGum newlyStarted = null;
531                lock.writeLock().lock();
532                try {
533                        var r = rainbowGum;
534                        if (r != null) {
535                                return r;
536                        }
537                        r = supplier.get();
538                        start(r);
539                        rainbowGum = r;
540                        newlyStarted = r;
541                        return r;
542
543                }
544                finally {
545                        lock.writeLock().unlock();
546                        /*
547                         * Published outside of the write lock so a subscriber can never deadlock or
548                         * trip the "tried to log too early" reentrancy guard above by, say, trying to
549                         * read a volatile field it owns - it is not calling back into this class.
550                         */
551                        if (newlyStarted != null) {
552                                globalChangePublisher.publish(newlyStarted);
553                        }
554                }
555
556        }
557
558        static boolean remove(@Nullable RainbowGum gum) {
559                lock.writeLock().lock();
560                try {
561                        var original = rainbowGum;
562                        if (gum != null) {
563                                if (original != gum) {
564                                        return false;
565                                }
566                        }
567                        /*
568                         * Reset the global router
569                         */
570                        if (original != null) {
571                                LogRouter.global().close();
572                        }
573                        rainbowGum = null;
574                        supplier = RainbowGumServiceProvider::provide;
575                        return true;
576                }
577                finally {
578                        lock.writeLock().unlock();
579                }
580        }
581
582        static void set(Supplier<RainbowGum> rainbowGumSupplier) {
583                Objects.requireNonNull(rainbowGumSupplier);
584                if (lock.writeLock().isHeldByCurrentThread()) {
585                        throw new IllegalStateException("RainbowGum component tried to log too early. "
586                                        + "This is usually caused by dependencies calling logging.");
587                }
588                lock.writeLock().lock();
589                try {
590                        rainbowGum = null;
591                        supplier = rainbowGumSupplier;
592                }
593                finally {
594                        lock.writeLock().unlock();
595                }
596        }
597
598        private static void start(RainbowGum gum) {
599                Objects.requireNonNull(gum);
600                ShutdownManager.addShutdownHook(gum);
601                gum.start();
602                InternalRootRouter.setRouter(gum.router());
603        }
604
605}
606
607/*
608 * Unlike LogConfig.ChangePublisher/LogRouter.RouteChangePublisher (both scoped to a
609 * single RainbowGum/router instance and torn down with it) this is a JVM-lifetime static
610 * registry, so consumers are held only weakly - otherwise every SLF4J logger factory (or
611 * any other subscriber) ever created over the life of the JVM, e.g. across many
612 * short-lived RainbowGums in tests, would be pinned forever.
613 */
614final class GlobalChangePublisher {
615
616        private final Queue<WeakReference<Consumer<RainbowGum>>> consumers = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();
617
618        void add(Consumer<RainbowGum> consumer) {
619                consumers.add(new WeakReference<>(consumer));
620        }
621
622        void publish(RainbowGum gum) {
623                for (var it = consumers.iterator(); it.hasNext();) {
624                        var consumer = it.next().get();
625                        if (consumer == null) {
626                                it.remove();
627                        }
628                        else {
629                                consumer.accept(gum);
630                        }
631                }
632        }
633
634}
635
636final class SimpleRainbowGum implements RainbowGum, Shutdownable {
637
638        private final LogConfig config;
639
640        private final RootRouter router;
641
642        private final AtomicInteger state = new AtomicInteger(0);
643
644        private final UUID instanceId;
645
646        private static final int INIT = 0;
647
648        private static final int STARTED = 1;
649
650        private static final int CLOSED = 2;
651
652        public SimpleRainbowGum(LogConfig config, RootRouter router, UUID instanceId) {
653                super();
654                this.config = config;
655                this.router = router;
656                this.instanceId = instanceId;
657        }
658
659        @Override
660        public LogConfig config() {
661                return this.config;
662        }
663
664        @Override
665        public RootRouter router() {
666                return this.router;
667        }
668
669        @Override
670        public RainbowGum start() {
671                int current;
672                if ((current = state.compareAndExchange(INIT, STARTED)) == INIT) {
673                        return RainbowGum.super.start();
674                }
675                throw new IllegalStateException("Cannot start. This rainbowgum is " + stateLabel(current));
676        }
677
678        @Override
679        public UUID instanceId() {
680                return this.instanceId;
681        }
682
683        @Override
684        public void close() {
685                if (state.compareAndSet(STARTED, CLOSED)) {
686                        RainbowGumHolder.remove(this);
687                        try {
688                                shutdown();
689                        }
690                        finally {
691                                ShutdownManager.removeShutdownHook(this);
692                        }
693                        return;
694                }
695        }
696
697        @Override
698        public void shutdown() {
699                router().close();
700                config().alerts().close();
701                config().serviceRegistry().close();
702        }
703
704        @Override
705        public String toString() {
706                return "SimpleRainbowGum [instanceId=" + instanceId + ", config=" + config + ", router=" + router + ", state="
707                                + stateLabel(state.get()) + "]";
708        }
709
710        private static String stateLabel(int state) {
711                return switch (state) {
712                        case INIT -> "created";
713                        case STARTED -> "started";
714                        case CLOSED -> "closed";
715                        default -> {
716                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("" + state);
717                        }
718                };
719        }
720
721}
